draft.title: Simultaneous equations by graphing
card: Simultaneous equations are two equations that must both be true at once. Each linear equation draws a straight line on the Cartesian plane.
Every point on a line makes that line's equation true. The point where the two lines cross is on both lines, so it makes both equations true.
To solve: graph both lines, read the crossing point (x, y), then check it by putting x and y into both equations.
Example: y = x + 1 and y = 7 − x. The lines cross at (3, 4). Check: 4 = 3 + 1 is true, and 7 − 3 = 4 is true. So x = 3 and y = 4.
draft.remember: The solution is the crossing point, and it must work in both equations.

a.q: Two lines cross at the point (2, 5). What is the solution of the pair of equations?
a.why: A point is written (x, y), so the first number is x and the second is y. Swapping them to x = 5 and y = 2 is a common mistake.
a.clue: A point is written in the order (x, y).

b.q: Lines y = 2x − 1 and y = x + 2 are graphed. Which point is where they cross?
b.why: At (3, 5): 2 × 3 − 1 = 5 and 3 + 2 = 5, so both equations are true. (1, 3) is on y = x + 2 only, and (2, 3) is on y = 2x − 1 only. (3, 4) fits neither line.
b.clue: Put each point into both equations. It must work in both.
